questions.question: What is Linux?

options.text: A paid operating system developed by Microsoft
An open-source operating system derived from Unix
A type of cloud service provided by AWS
A programming language for scripting

explanation.correct: Linux is a free, open-source operating system derived from Unix, created by Linus Torvalds in 1991.
explanation.why: A is Windows. C is incorrect — Linux is an OS, not a cloud service. D is incorrect — Linux is an OS, not a language.

questions.question: Which of the following is the core component of the Linux operating system?

options.text: Shell
Kernel
File System
All of the above

explanation.correct: Linux architecture consists of the Kernel, Shell, File System, and GNU utilities — all are core components.
explanation.why: Each component plays a distinct role. Choosing any one alone would be incomplete.

questions.question: What is the role of the Linux Kernel?

options.text: Provides a user interface for commands
Manages hardware resources and acts as a bridge between software and hardware
Stores files in an organized hierarchy
Interprets shell scripts

explanation.correct: The Kernel is the core of Linux — it manages CPU, memory, I/O, and acts as the bridge between applications and hardware.
explanation.why: A describes the Shell. C describes the File System. D also describes the Shell/Bash interpreter.

questions.question: What does the Shell do in Linux?

options.text: Directly manages hardware resources
Acts as the interpreter between user commands and the kernel
Stores user data permanently
Provides a graphical interface

explanation.correct: The Shell acts as an interpreter — it takes commands from the user and passes them to the kernel for execution.
explanation.why: A is the Kernel's job. C is the File System. D describes a GUI, which Linux primarily avoids.

questions.question: What is Bash?

options.text: A Linux distribution
A type of kernel module
The default command-line interpreter (shell) for Linux
A cloud service by AWS

explanation.correct: Bash (Bourne Again SHell) is the most common shell in Linux, used to interpret and run user commands.
explanation.why: A is incorrect — Ubuntu, CentOS etc. are distros. B is incorrect — it is not a kernel module. D is unrelated.

questions.question: Linux is a combination of which two components?

options.text: Windows + Unix
Linux Kernel + GNU utilities
Shell + File System
Bash + Python

explanation.correct: Linux = Linux Kernel + GNU utilities. The GNU project provides the tools and utilities that make the OS functional.
explanation.why: Unix is a separate OS. Shell and File System are components within Linux, not the full combination.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to connect to a Linux EC2 instance from a remote client?

options.text: RDP
FTP
SSH
HTTP

explanation.correct: SSH (Secure Shell) is used to connect to Linux-based servers remotely, including Linux EC2 instances on AWS.
explanation.why: RDP is for Windows. FTP is for file transfer. HTTP is a web protocol, not a remote shell protocol.

questions.question: What is EC2 Instance Connect?

options.text: A way to connect to EC2 via FTP
An AWS-provided browser-based SSH connection to Linux EC2 instances
A VPN tunnel into an EC2 instance
A method to connect to Windows EC2 using a browser

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Connect provides a browser-based SSH session to Linux EC2 instances directly from the AWS console.
explanation.why: FTP is unrelated. VPN is not used here. EC2 Instance Connect is only available for Linux, not Windows.

questions.question: When would you use EC2 Instance Connect instead of an SSH client?

options.text: When you want faster performance than SSH
When you don't have a key pair and want to connect via AWS console
When the instance is Windows-based
When you need to transfer files to the instance

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Connect is useful when you don't have a key pair or when you want a quick browser-based SSH session from the console.
explanation.why: It doesn't offer faster performance. It's only for Linux. File transfer uses SCP or SFTP.

questions.question: What is the default username for Amazon Linux EC2 instances?

options.text: root
admin
ubuntu
ec2-user

explanation.correct: The default username for Amazon Linux-based EC2 instances is ec2-user.
explanation.why: root is the superuser account. ubuntu is the default for Ubuntu-based instances. admin is used on some Debian instances.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the Linux File System?

options.text: A software that interprets user commands
A hierarchical structure starting from root (/) that organizes all files
A cloud storage system managed by AWS
The graphical interface for managing files

explanation.correct: The Linux File System is a hierarchical structure starting from / (root), where all files and directories are organized.
explanation.why: A describes the Shell. C is S3. D describes a GUI file manager, which Linux doesn't rely on.

questions.question: Why is Linux preferred over Windows for servers in enterprise environments?

options.text: Linux has a better graphical interface
Linux is free, open-source, faster, and more secure
Linux supports more commercial software
Linux requires no configuration

explanation.correct: Linux is preferred because it is free to use, open-source, performs faster than Windows for server workloads, and is highly secure without needing antivirus software.
explanation.why: Windows has a better GUI. Linux has fewer commercial apps. All OS require configuration.

questions.question: What is the Linux command to print the current working directory?

options.text: ls
cd
pwd
mkdir

explanation.correct: pwd (Print Working Directory) displays the full path of the current directory you are in.
explanation.why: ls lists files. cd changes directories. mkdir creates directories.

questions.question: How do you navigate one directory up in Linux?

options.text: cd /
cd ..
cd -
ls ..

explanation.correct: cd .. moves you one directory up (to the parent directory) in Linux.
explanation.why: cd / goes to root. cd - goes to the previous directory. ls .. just lists the parent without navigating.

questions.question: What is the difference between the root user and ec2-user in Linux?

options.text: No difference — both are the same account
Root has full superuser privileges; ec2-user is a standard login account for Amazon Linux
ec2-user has more permissions than root
Root is only for GUI access; ec2-user is for CLI

explanation.correct: Root is the superuser with unrestricted access. ec2-user is the default non-root login account on Amazon Linux instances.
explanation.why: They are distinct accounts. ec2-user has limited permissions unless elevated with sudo. Root is not GUI-only.

questions.question: What does 'open-source' mean in the context of Linux?

options.text: Linux can only be used by businesses
Anyone can view, modify, and distribute the source code
Linux is freely available only for academic use
Linux can be modified only by Linus Torvalds

explanation.correct: Open-source means the source code is publicly available — anyone can view, modify, and redistribute it under the license terms.
explanation.why: Open-source has no business or academic restriction. Anyone can contribute, not just the creator.

questions.question: What is a Linux distribution (distro)?

options.text: A version of the Linux Kernel only
A packaged OS combining the Linux Kernel with software, package managers, and tools
A type of AWS instance
A shell scripting language

explanation.correct: A Linux distribution is a complete OS built on the Linux Kernel plus additional software, package managers, desktop environments, and tools (e.g., Ubuntu, CentOS, Amazon Linux).
explanation.why: A distro is not just the kernel. It's not an AWS instance type or a scripting language.

questions.question: What is the purpose of GNU utilities in Linux?

options.text: They provide the kernel that manages hardware
They provide essential command-line tools and programs that make Linux usable
They provide the graphical desktop environment
They handle network connectivity

explanation.correct: GNU utilities provide essential tools like ls, cp, mv, grep, and many more that make a Linux system functional beyond just the kernel.
explanation.why: The kernel handles hardware. Desktop environments (like GNOME) handle graphics. Network is managed by different subsystems.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key reason Linux does NOT require antivirus software?

options.text: Linux has no internet connectivity
Linux has a strict permission model and process isolation that limits malware spread
Viruses cannot run on any Unix-based OS
AWS blocks all viruses for Linux instances

explanation.correct: Linux's security model — strict file permissions, user isolation, and root access restrictions — makes it inherently resistant to malware spread.
explanation.why: Linux does have internet access. Unix-based systems can be targeted, but the architecture limits impact. AWS doesn't block viruses automatically.

questions.question: What is the relationship between SSH and EC2 Instance Connect?

options.text: They are completely different protocols with no relation
EC2 Instance Connect uses SSH under the hood but manages the connection from the AWS console
EC2 Instance Connect replaces SSH entirely and is more secure
SSH is only for Windows; EC2 Instance Connect is for Linux

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Connect uses the SSH protocol internally — it just handles key management and browser-based session initiation for you.
explanation.why: They are related through SSH. Neither fully replaces the other. SSH is for Linux; RDP is for Windows.

questions.question: A team wants to connect to a Linux EC2 instance but has lost their private key. What is the BEST solution?

options.text: Terminate and relaunch the instance with a new key pair
Use EC2 Instance Connect from the AWS console (if no key pair was set)
Connect via RDP using IAM credentials
SSH without any key using just the username

explanation.correct: If the instance was launched without a key pair or using EC2 Instance Connect's own key management, you can connect directly from the AWS console.
explanation.why: Terminating loses data unless EBS is preserved. RDP is for Windows. SSH without a key is insecure and won't work by default.

questions.question: What happens to EC2 instances and data created inside an AWS Canvas (training) lab environment when you end the lab session?

options.text: Instances persist permanently in your real AWS account
Instances are saved in a snapshot automatically
Everything is deleted — the lab is a temporary session that resets on end
Instances move to stopped state and resume on next login

explanation.correct: AWS Canvas lab environments are temporary sessions. When a lab ends, all created resources are automatically deleted — nothing carries over to a real AWS account.
explanation.why: Labs are sandboxed environments, not connected to your real AWS account. No snapshots are auto-created.

questions.question: In Linux architecture, which layer sits directly above the hardware?

options.text: Shell
Applications
Kernel
GNU Libraries

explanation.correct: The Kernel is the layer directly above hardware — it abstracts hardware resources and provides system calls to upper layers.
explanation.why: Applications are at the top. Shell sits between the user and kernel. GNU libraries sit above the kernel but below the shell in some models.

questions.question: A company needs a low-cost, highly secure server OS for running web applications at scale. Which choice is most appropriate?

options.text: Windows Server with RDP
Linux (Amazon Linux 2) with SSH access
macOS running on EC2
Linux with antivirus installed

explanation.correct: Amazon Linux 2 is optimized for EC2, free to use, highly secure, and ideal for scalable web application servers.
explanation.why: Windows Server adds licensing cost. macOS is not available on EC2. Linux does not need antivirus — adding it is unnecessary overhead.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between connecting to a Linux EC2 instance vs a Windows EC2 instance?

options.text: Linux uses HTTP; Windows uses HTTPS
Linux uses SSH (port 22); Windows uses RDP (port 3389)
Linux requires a GUI; Windows uses CLI
Both use the same RDP protocol

explanation.correct: Linux EC2 uses SSH on port 22 for remote access. Windows EC2 uses RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) on port 3389.
explanation.why: HTTP/HTTPS are web protocols. Linux is primarily CLI-based, not GUI. RDP is exclusively for Windows remote desktop.

questions.question: Which Linux component is responsible for process management and memory allocation?

options.text: Shell
GNU Tools
Kernel
Bash Interpreter

explanation.correct: The Kernel manages all system resources — including process scheduling, memory allocation, and I/O management.
explanation.why: Shell interprets commands. GNU Tools are utilities. Bash is a shell, which sends requests to the kernel for execution.

questions.question: What does 'derived from Unix' mean in the context of Linux?

options.text: Linux is a direct copy of Unix source code
Linux was designed following Unix principles and philosophy but is an independent implementation
Linux runs Unix applications natively without modification
Linux and Unix share the same kernel

explanation.correct: Linux was designed inspired by Unix principles (portability, modularity, simplicity) but was written from scratch as an independent, open-source kernel by Linus Torvalds.
explanation.why: Linux did not copy Unix code. Not all Unix apps run on Linux natively. They have separate kernels.

questions.question: Why is Linux faster than Windows for server workloads?

options.text: Linux has a more modern programming language
Linux has a lightweight architecture with no mandatory GUI overhead
Linux uses faster hardware by default
Linux has more RAM available

explanation.correct: Linux servers run without a GUI (headless), consuming fewer resources. Its lightweight architecture allows more system resources to be dedicated to actual workloads.
explanation.why: Language choice is not the reason. Hardware is identical. RAM is not inherently more on Linux — it's just not wasted on GUI processes.

questions.question: A student launches an EC2 instance without selecting a key pair. Which connection method should they use?

options.text: SSH from terminal using any username
RDP from any machine
EC2 Instance Connect from the AWS console
VPN tunnel into the instance

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Connect is the appropriate method when no key pair was used — it manages the temporary SSH key internally and provides a browser-based terminal.
explanation.why: SSH without a key pair is not possible by default. RDP is for Windows. VPN is unrelated to initial instance access.

questions.question: In an AWS training lab environment (Canvas), a student starts a lab, creates an S3 bucket, then exits midway. The next day they restart the lab. What is the state of their S3 bucket?

options.text: The bucket still exists and contains all files
The bucket exists but is empty
The bucket no longer exists — the lab environment was reset
The bucket was moved to the student's real AWS account

explanation.correct: Canvas lab environments are fully temporary. When a session ends (even midway), a cleanup process runs and removes all created resources. The next session starts completely fresh.
explanation.why: Nothing persists between Canvas lab sessions. Resources do not transfer to real AWS accounts.
